 Print A startling banner has emerged in Lal Chowk, Srinagar, seeking information about four terrorists SRINAGAR: A banner seeking information about the whereabouts of four terrorists wanted by security forces surfaced in Srinagar’s Lal Chowk area on Sunday. A flex banner was found hanging in the Pratap Park area, seeking information about four terrorists, including Mohammad Lateef Bhat, who is believed to be active in South Kashmir. The other three names on the banner were Bilal Ahmad Mir, Mohammad Umar Mir and Abid Qayoom Lone. All three are from Baramulla district in north Kashmir and are currently believed to be in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK). The banner stated: “Anyone who can provide credible information regarding the movement/presence of these terrorists, the identity of the informant will be kept strictly confidential and a handsome reward will be given for reliable information.” It also provided four contact numbers. Police have not issued any statement about the banner so far. On October 5, J&K Police IG Kashmir Sujit Kumar had said that Kashmir had only one active local terrorist and that recruitment in the Valley had completely stopped this year. The police had identified the lone local terrorist as Mohammad Lateef Bhat, a resident of Khrewan Chader village in south Kashmir’s Kulgam district. A reward of Rs 15 lakh was announced in August for information leading to his arrest. Bhat is accused of killing a head constable and two migrant workers in separate attacks in Anantnag and Kulgam in July. He is believed to have joined terrorist ranks last year.
